name_reason: Name follows the fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> game-function convention (battle domain; descriptor check_char_is_dead) and accurately reflects the logic: it returns the runtime char's dead bit (flags bit0) as 0 alive / 1 dead. It is the read counterpart to fd2_mark_char_as_dead @ 0x32975 (writes flags = 1), and the symmetric naming is correct. No Ghidra address residue in the name.
purpose: Return whether a runtime-array character is dead: extracts bit0 (CHARFLAG_DEAD) of runtime_char[char_idx].flags as 0 (alive) or 1 (dead).
logic_summary: __CHK(4) stack-probe at entry (4-byte frame). Then: EDX = char_idx*0x50 (runtime_char stride), EAX = deref of runtime_char array pointer at [0x53A45], AL = byte [EAX+EDX+0x5] (the flags field at runtime_char offset +0x05), AL &= 0x01, MOVZX EAX,AL. Equivalent to: return data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr[char_idx].flags & CHARFLAG_DEAD. Cyclomatic complexity 1 (no branches).

params.name: char_idx
params.semantics: Index into the runtime character array (data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr; stride 0x50 bytes). Body uses it directly as the array subscript; callers pass loop indices over 0..party_member_count-1 (e.g. fd2_build_dead_chars_list_for_revive iterates menu_party_member_count) and specific unit ids in chapter post-action / event handlers. In Ghidra the parameter is still the generic placeholder param_1; src already names it char_idx.

returns.semantics: 0 = char is alive, 1 = char is dead. Value is runtime_char[char_idx].flags & 0x01 (CHARFLAG_DEAD), zero-extended. Callers compare it against == 1 / == 0 / use it as a truth value.
